issues.legal_issue: A pre-emption decree based on an intermediary’s proprietary interest cannot be executed for possession after that interest has vested in the State and ceased to exist.
material_facts: A co-sharer obtained a pre-emption decree concerning a share in land and deposited the sale consideration before the land reform law took effect in the area.
The vendees remained in possession, so the decree-holder later sought execution to obtain possession.
Before execution was sought, the proprietary interests in the land had vested in the State, leaving the former proprietors with no surviving interest on which to base execution.
issues.conclusion: The pre-emption decree was incapable of execution because the proprietary interests on which it was based had ceased to exist upon vesting in the State.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 4 and 6(a) of the U.P. Zamindari Abolition and Land Reforms Act, 1950, intermediary rights, title and interest in the land vest in the State and cease to exist. A decree based on those former rights cannot be executed after they have lapsed, even without an express provision invalidating the decree. Rana Sheo Ambar Singh v. Allahabad Bank Ltd. held that, absent the special remedy under section 6(h), a mortgage decree had nothing to proceed against once the former proprietary rights were extinguished; section 6(h), read with section 73 of the Transfer of Property Act, provided a remedy against compensation money. That reasoning answers the claim that the pre-emption decree survived. Shivashankar Prasad Shah v. Baikunth Nath Singh followed Rana Sheo Ambar Singh. The court expressed no opinion on any rights that might arise under section 18, and noted that Kailash Rai v. Jai Jai Ram concerned the meaning of possession under that section.

rule.if: preemption_decree_execution and decree_based_on_former_proprietary_right and land_proprietary_rights_vested_in_state and former_proprietary_rights_ceased and possession_still_required

predicates.preemption_decree_execution: The proceeding seeks to execute a decree granting pre-emption of an interest in land.
predicates.decree_based_on_former_proprietary_right: The decree rests on a claimant’s former proprietary interest in the land.
predicates.land_proprietary_rights_vested_in_state: The land’s proprietary rights vested in the State before execution was sought.
predicates.former_proprietary_rights_ceased: The former proprietary rights on which the decree depended ceased to exist, with no such rights surviving in the decree-holder.
predicates.possession_still_required: The decree-holder still needed execution to obtain possession of the land.

issues.definition: When execution of a pre-emption decree based on former proprietary rights is sought after those rights have vested in the State and ceased to exist, while possession remains to be obtained, the decree is incapable of execution.
